frame.objective: Find out whether any consumer group offers Moldex a worthwhile new business before committing money
constraints: Hearing protectors may fall under strict PPE rules
alternatives: Supply venues and event operators as a business customer
Stay with workplace customers and do not enter

searches: music events ear plugs use trial availability
hyperacusis do not wear earplugs all the time

T1.claim: Appearance holds back use among concert-goers, so a discreet redesign would open a consumer segment for an industrial maker.
T1.who_benefits: People who attend loud music events and avoid visible earplugs
T1.why_behaviour_changes: Embarrassment falls when the product does not look like workwear, so they keep it in.
T1.how_value_is_captured: A branded product sold at a higher price per pair than bulk workplace plugs
assumptions: Embarrassment, not forgetting, is what stops wearing
predictions: Observed wearing is higher for a discreet design than for a plain plug when both are available at the same price

T2.claim: People do not wear protection because it is not to hand at the moment of need, so supply through venues matters more than redesign.
T2.who_benefits: Event-goers who did not plan ahead, and venues that want to protect audiences
T2.why_behaviour_changes: A prompt and a plug at the door turn a forgotten intention into use.
T2.how_value_is_captured: Bulk sales to venue operators, close to how the company already sells through business buyers
assumptions: Venues will pay for or stock plugs
Forgetting explains more non-use than dislike does
predictions: Observed wearing is higher where plugs are offered at the door than where the same plugs are only sold online beforehand

T3.claim: Sleepers have a stronger recurring need than concert-goers, so foam plugs for sleep are a better first consumer market than music.
T3.who_benefits: Adults whose sleep is disturbed by noise
T3.why_behaviour_changes: Disturbed sleep is felt every night, so the problem reminds them to buy again.
T3.how_value_is_captured: Repeat purchases of low-cost foam plugs through retail or online
assumptions: Foam plugs made for workers can be comfortable overnight
predictions: The repeat purchase rate is higher for sleep buyers than for music buyers over the same period

X1.name: Door offer against discreet design at small venues
X1.method: At matched events, offer either plain plugs at the door, discreet plugs at the door, or plain plugs online beforehand. Observers count who is wearing protection.
X1.sample: About 12 events with observers at each
X1.measure: Share of attendees observed wearing protection

prediction_by_theory.T1: Discreet plugs at the door beat plain plugs at the door
prediction_by_theory.T2: Both door arms beat online, with no gap between discreet and plain

X1.decision_rule: Pursue venue supply if door arms beat online by at least 5 points and the design gap is under 2 points

final.recommendation: Do not launch a consumer brand yet. Test venue supply first, because it is closest to how Moldex already sells and the evidence for availability is the strongest, though bundled with prompting.
final.target_customer: Venue and event operators first, for people who attend loud events
final.value_proposition: Protection available at the moment of need, supplied by a trusted workplace maker
final.next_action: Run the door offer test at small venues before any product redesign
final.uncertainty: No study separates availability from prompting, economics are unknown, and venue willingness to pay is untested
would_change_if: Discreet plugs clearly beat plain plugs at the door
Venues refuse to stock or pay for plugs
